ownershipReviews.decision: Semantically a library; migrate only after consumer audit
ownershipReviews.rationale: Generic clone registry/diff/progress with no event subscriptions or flavor gate; preserve global/getter/API semantics.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/inventory/inventory.lua owns counts and consumer-supplied material arithmetic
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Inventory owns items/material counts; Equipment owns equipped state; Professions owns recipe domain state
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not merge item counts, equipment and recipes
ownershipReviews.rationale: Prevent a single items god-module and keep consumer recipe selection outside Inventory.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/combat/combat.lua owns combat state and narrow callbacks
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Combat for combat state; Encounters for encounter metadata/timeline; Instances for lockouts/difficulty
ownershipReviews.decision: Extend Combat only for intrinsic combat signals
ownershipReviews.rationale: EncounterJournal, live encounter state and instance lockouts are distinct domains.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: No general Units owner; Auras/Combat/compat hold narrow unit operations
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Research a Units identity/state owner; keep Cast and specialized state separate
ownershipReviews.decision: Resolve unit identity, health/power secrecy and token comparability before APIs
ownershipReviews.rationale: Avoid duplicating Cast, Auras, Range, Group and Nameplate state.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/auras/auras.lua owns aura state and specific readiness
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Auras for aura state; Spells for spell metadata/cooldowns; Dispels for classification only if justified
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not turn Auras into a general Spells or ActionBars owner
ownershipReviews.rationale: Current CastReadiness is a narrow contract, not full cast or spell state.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: Core has narrow party/raid helpers; no LFG owner
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Group for party/raid; Guild for guild/club; LFG as a separate queue domain if needed
ownershipReviews.decision: Separate roster, guild and queue state
ownershipReviews.rationale: Permissions, async state and lifecycle differ across these domains.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: modules/worldmap/worldmap.lua owns coordinates, pins and nearest-place lookup
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: WorldMap for map geometry/pins; Travel for taxi/navigation/summons only with consumer need
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not substitute geometric distance for spell range or taxi state
ownershipReviews.rationale: Map navigation, spell range and protected travel actions are different capabilities.

ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Quest for quest state; Guides for guide/journal/tutorial content only if required
ownershipReviews.decision: Keep progression data separate from presentation guides
ownershipReviews.rationale: AdventureJournal and Tutorial references are incomplete and do not justify a guide runtime by themselves.

ownershipReviews.currentOwner: SharedMedia generic paths; Fonts/Textures/Sound specialized registries; Colors/Design color ownership
ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: SharedMedia for generic discovery/interoperability; specialized libraries for metadata/behavior
ownershipReviews.decision: Do not create an automatic unified mirror of specialized registries
ownershipReviews.rationale: SharedMedia scans sound only; Fonts, Textures and Sound own their specialized handles/defaults/application.

ownershipReviews.recommendedOwner: Evaluate one serialization/data owner; charts belong in UI and keybinding controls in UI with Core registration
ownershipReviews.decision: Consolidate supporting capabilities instead of creating one directory per noun
ownershipReviews.rationale: The candidate count is not a mandate for new public namespaces.

replacementMatrix.rationale: One framework instance and registry; no LibStub version negotiation.
Declarative addon factory and lifecycle, not API-compatible emulation.
Central event/message/emitter dispatch.
Budgeted After/Every/CancelTimer driver.
Central secure post-hook owner.
Central slash registration.
Profiles, migrations and SavedVariables adoption.
Options and profile-aware controls, not an AceConfig compatibility layer.
Declarative options with existing UI composition.
Reusable widgets exist; complete AceGUI widget coverage is not claimed.
Framework-owned locale registry and overrides.
Failure-isolated messages and emitters.
Generic pack/path registration and interoperability; specialized behavior remains separate.
Observable data objects and notifications.
Minimap and compartment buttons.
Nested/native menu composition.
Countdown/progress components.
Map coordinates/pins exist; comprehensive HereBeDragons compatibility is not claimed.
General table serialization exists in Core; broader transport compatibility is not claimed.
Scoped opt-in latest-per-key bucketing with regression and burst evidence; not a universal AceBucket replacement.
Requires a real consumer and channel contract.
Throttling belongs to the communication owner.
Queue discipline belongs to the communication owner.
Differential sync and recovery are not implemented.
Core table serialization exists; a general LibSerialize-compatible surface is not claimed.
No compression owner is implemented.
Animation composition remains research.
Button glow belongs to the same animation research owner.
The shipped custom drag editor is not native Edit Mode integration.
Composed tooltips exist; LibQTip compatibility is not claimed.
Notification routing remains research.
Sink routing belongs to the same notification owner.
Theme/skin mechanisms exist; full Masque replacement is not claimed.
Display owns positioned elements; general frame discovery is not a separate public library.
Search contract and consumer are not established.
Query construction belongs to the same search owner.
Range semantics and secrecy require research; map distance is not a substitute.
Spell/action range needs one domain owner.
Spell metadata scope and native API differences are unresolved.
Talent/loadout models vary by client.
Group inspection and roster state need a bounded owner.
Do not create parallel group and communication contracts without a consumer.
Healing prediction and restricted values require native evidence.
Aura classification and protected dispel actions are separate concerns.
Secure action-button behavior is not implied by spell queries.
Travel data belongs in a provenance-controlled data pack.
Static quest data requires provenance and refresh rules.
Reusable components are a candidate, not an oUF-compatible runtime.

implementationSequence.rationale: Establish source-of-truth ownership and evidence before runtime expansion; delivered by this Phase 0 change.
Delivered scoped opt-in latest-per-key bucketing with ordering, payload, failure, cancellation and 10,000-event burst evidence.
Semantically justified but blocked on consumer audit and synchronized public-contract migration.
Interface expansion follows Core/resource ownership and requires a real long-list consumer and allocation benchmark.
Harden and scope the existing Core table serializer before any transport design; do not create a parallel owner.
Communication follows serialization and a maintained consumer rather than speculative transport APIs.
